import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Filter data for a specific analysis: count of dogs by breed and gender

# Create a bar plot

sns.barplot(data=breed_gender_counts, x='Rasse1Text', y='AnzHunde', hue='SexLang', palette='viridis')

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Number of Dogs by Breed and Gender in Zurich', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Dog Breed', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=14)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.legend(title='Gender', fontsize=12)

```python
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Filter data for a specific analysis: count of dogs by breed and gender
breed_gender_counts = data.groupby(['Rasse1Text', 'SexLang']).agg({'AnzHunde': 'sum'}).reset_index()

# Create a bar plot
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))
sns.barplot(data=breed_gender_counts, x='Rasse1Text', y='AnzHunde', hue='SexLang', palette='viridis')

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Number of Dogs by Breed and Gender in Zurich', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Dog Breed', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=14)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.legend(title='Gender', fontsize=12)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
```
